title: 6 Yim Si-wan K-dramas to revisit during “Love in Disguise” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao October 23, 2026 After gaining international recognition through "Squid Game," Yim Si-wan is keeping the momentum going with "Love in Disguise." Starring opposite Seol In-ah, he plays Yoon Yi-jun, a wealthy chaebol heir suspected of murder, whose life gets complicated when a female detective disguises herself as his male secretary to investigate him. From charming romantic leads and awkward office rookies to unsettling characters and comedic roles, Yim has shown his versatility time and again. While waiting for the next episode of "Love in Disguise," here are six of his K-dramas worth revisiting 
 Squid Game Seasons 2-3 (2024-2025)
 Joining Netflix's global phenomenon in its second season, Yim Si-wan takes on one of his most controversial roles as Lee Myung-gi, a former cryptocurrency influencer known as Player 333. After a disastrous investment scheme leaves him and his followers in financial ruin, he enters the deadly competition hoping to turn his fortunes around. Things get even messier when he encounters his pregnant ex-girlfriend, Jun-hee (Jo Yu-ri), among the contestants. As the games become increasingly ruthless, Myung-gi's selfish choices reveal just how far he is willing to go to survive, earning him a reputation as a “global villain” among viewers.
 Run On (2020)
 For a softer side of Yim Si-wan, Run On is well worth revisiting. He plays Ki Seon-gyeom, a national track athlete who walks away from his sporting career after standing up for a bullied teammate. As he figures out life beyond the running track, he meets Oh Mi-joo (Shin Se-kyung), a film subtitle translator who eventually becomes his interpreter. Despite their different personalities, the two gradually find themselves falling for each other. Through their slow-burning romance and heartfelt conversations, Seon-gyeom learns to express his feelings, make his own choices and embrace a new chapter in life.

 Misaeng: Incomplete Life (2014)
 Long before becoming a familiar leading man, Yim Si-wan made his acting breakthrough with Misaeng: Incomplete Life . He plays Jang Geu-rae, a former aspiring professional baduk player who lands an internship at a major trading company despite having little experience or formal qualifications. Thrown into the demanding corporate world, he struggles to keep up with his more accomplished colleagues while gradually applying lessons from baduk to tackle workplace challenges. With guidance from his manager Oh Sang-shik (Lee Sung-min), Geu-rae slowly finds his footing in a drama that captures the everyday frustrations, small victories and realities of office life.
 Strangers from Hell (2019)
 Taking a much darker turn, Yim Si-wan stars in the psychological thriller Strangers from Hell as Yoon Jong-woo, an aspiring writer who moves to Seoul for a new job. With little money to spare, he settles into a rundown residence called Eden Studio, only to discover that his neighbours are anything but ordinary. Among them is Seo Moon-jo (Lee Dong-wook), a seemingly friendly dentist who takes an unsettling interest in him. As mysterious disappearances and disturbing incidents begin to unfold, Jong-woo finds himself trapped in a growing nightmare, with his paranoia and sanity pushed to the limit.
 Boyhood (2023)
 Switching things up with comedy, Yim Si-wan takes on a completely different character in Boyhood , a coming-of-age series set in 1989 South Korea. He plays Jang Byeong-tae, a timid high school student who transfers to a new school hoping to leave his bullying troubles behind. But thanks to a case of mistaken identity, he is suddenly hailed as the legendary fighter known as the White Tiger of Asan, becoming the school's most feared student overnight. While he enjoys his newfound popularity, keeping up the act becomes increasingly difficult, especially when the real fighter arrives.
 Summer Strike (2022)
 If you're in the mood for something comforting, Summer Strike offers a gentler side of Yim Si-wan. Starring opposite Seolhyun, he plays Ahn Dae-beom, a shy librarian and former maths prodigy living in a quiet seaside village. His peaceful routine begins to change when Lee Yeo-reum, a burned-out office worker, quits her job and moves to the village in search of a fresh start. As the two slowly grow closer, they help each other confront past traumas and rediscover life's simple pleasures, although unexpected mysteries soon threaten their newfound peace.
